rubrics.criterion: The refactor makes the class that owns the shared expansion state (the foldable model) responsible for interpreting that state again: the derived-height rule (0px when collapsed, measured fixed height while transitioning, auto otherwise), the measure-then-expand choreography (temporary expansion with transitions disabled and a synchronous layout read), the completion bookkeeping (releasing the fixed height and completing), and the expanded/completed class distinction are implemented by the state-owning model class or by a component that the model itself owns and exposes, rather than remaining encoded in consumer code.
rubrics.rationale: This case's smell is behavior that reads and writes the foldable's reactive keys living in folder/color/point-2d consumers; the ground truth of repair is that the interpretation of those keys lives with the data owner, in whatever sound design the solver chooses.

rubrics.criterion: The credited consumer classes no longer re-implement the expansion rules from the raw state keys: the folder controller, the color view/controller, and the point-2d controller each contain only locally justified wiring (event subscription, DOM element references, focus/blur handling), and their reactive-state interpretation volume no longer concentrates on the foldable's data.
rubrics.rationale: The checker credits exactly the consumer methods whose reactive-state operation volume concentrates on the foldable; this rubric verifies the corresponding code-level outcome of the repair across every credited class, not just a lowered match count.

rubrics.criterion: The refactor is not a hollow relocation: the body of the state interpretation has not merely been moved into module-level procedure functions (or other units outside the data owner) that still read and write the raw keys while the state-owning class remains a behaviorless key-value container.
rubrics.rationale: In this case a purely syntactic move (extracting the consumer methods as free functions) would silence the structural relation without restoring data locality; the state owner must regain the behavior for the repair to be real.

rubrics.criterion: All three inline consumer code paths (folder blade, color inline picker, point-2d inline pad) are rewired to the consolidated owner behavior with an equivalent subscription lifecycle: an initial application at construction, the before-change measurement flow, application on change, completion on transitionend, and the folder's forced completion when child blades are added or removed.
rubrics.rationale: The completion-on-rack-mutation behavior is unique to the folder consumer and easy to lose when centralizing; this fact pins that each component's specific wiring was translated, not only the first one found.

rubrics.criterion: The consolidated rules are exposed through one coherent owner surface (such as model methods, getters, or an owner-provided binding helper) that all three components integrate with in the same way, rather than through ad-hoc hooks that differ per component for the same operation.
rubrics.rationale: The injected state has three drifted shapes for the same rules; a good repair removes not only the duplication but also the drift, which is the maintenance win this case models.

rubrics.criterion: The patch removes what the refactor made obsolete: unused imports (for example transition/element helper functions), stale event subscriptions, private handler members, and derived-value seams that no longer have callers are all deleted rather than left dormant in the touched modules.
rubrics.rationale: The refactor deletes consumer-side interpretation code; this instance-specific cleanup obligation prevents the common half-done repair that leaves the old blocks in place, dead but readable.

rubrics.criterion: No per-component copies or near-copies of the expansion rule logic remain anywhere in the patch's final state: supporting blocks that only served the old design (duplicated completion juggling, per-view class-sync duplicates, leftover measurement helpers) are gone or reduced to genuine wiring, with no duplicate implementations left behind dead flags or unused subscriptions.
rubrics.rationale: The change spans six production files; a solver may fix the credited classes but leave the supporting cohorts of the same rules behind, which would keep the drift the maintenance task complains about.

rubrics.criterion: The expansion animation semantics survive the refactor: collapsing still yields a 0px height, expanding still animates to a measured fixed height via the temporary-measure flow (transitions disabled around the synchronous layout read, temporary state restored before animating), 'auto' height is used when unfixed, and expansions whose height cannot produce a transitionend (empty folders, rack contents changing) still end up completed.
rubrics.rationale: The temporal choreography is the behaviorally fragile core of this case; these are the case-specific regressions a plausible incomplete refactor would introduce while the suite stays mostly green.

rubrics.criterion: The non-inline behaviors and contracts stay intact: popup-layout pickers keep mirroring the expanded state without animating an inline height, expanded/completed CSS classes are applied and removed exactly as before (including on initial render), and the visible API surface is unchanged (folder expanded property, color/point-2d expanded and pickerLayout params, folder state import/export).
rubrics.rationale: The refactor touches two layout modes and the state import path; this fact checks the compatibility boundary this case explicitly promises to keep stable.

rubrics.criterion: Focus and keyboard behavior of the inline pickers is preserved: expanding a picker focuses its first focusable element, and Escape from the picker returns focus to the trigger button, without the class/view reshuffling changing focus targets.
rubrics.rationale: Focus management lives in the same consumer methods being reshaped; it is the least test-covered behavior in this area and a plausible silent regression specific to this task.
